chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ibn Muskhan, from Isma'il ibn Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him, 'We give the man the dirhams, and I stipulate upon him that he give them in another land, black (fresh/unworn), by their weight, and I stipulate that condition upon him.' He said, 'There is no harm (in it).'

key_terms.أَشْتَرِطُ: I stipulate / I make a condition
key_terms.سُوداً: Black (referring to fresh, unworn, or high-quality coins)
key_terms.لاَ بَأْسَ: There is no harm / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to stipulate the delivery location and condition of coins in a financial transaction?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the stipulation of delivering silver dirhams in a different location as fresh, full-weight coins, illustrating the flexibility in conditional sales (bay' al-shart) within Shia jurisprudence. It highlights the principle that specific delivery conditions do not invalidate the contract, provided the core elements of the exchange remain intact. This ruling is foundational for understanding modern financial stipulations regarding location and condition of goods in Islamic commercial law.
